PM assures support for waste-to-fuel technology
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday assured support for a technology that could turn waste into fuel oil and help reduce Bangladesh’s dependence on imported energy.
He gave the assurance as a team of researchers led by Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (Kuet) Professor Dr Md Khalequzzaman briefed him on the technology at his office in Tejgaon, said a release issued by the PM’s Press Wing.
The technology uses a process known as hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) to convert human waste, waste from sewage treatment plants, kitchen waste and agricultural residues into fuel oil.
The researchers said they have been working on the technology for around 10 years and have achieved a 50–55% biocrude yield in laboratory tests. They have also made progress in producing biocrude with a high diesel content.
The next step is to set up a pilot plant capable of processing one to three tons of waste daily to assess the technology’s efficiency, production costs and commercial viability. The estimated cost of the pilot project is Tk100–120 crore.
According to the researchers, the technology, if developed for commercial-scale production, could replace around 10–15% of imported crude oil and save foreign currency equivalent to Tk6,500–13,000 crore annually.
However, the estimates would need to be validated through large-scale technical and economic assessments, they said.
The researchers said the technology could also help reduce environmental pollution, improve waste management and create opportunities for developing a domestic fuel industry.
The Prime Minister assured them of the government’s necessary cooperation in advancing the initiative.
Power and Energy Minister Iqbal Mahmood Tuku, State Minister Anindya Islam Amit, University Grants Commission member Professor Abdullah Al Mamun, Kuet Vice-Chancellor Professor Mohammad Masud and Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation Chairman Dr Mohammad Rafiqul Islam were present at the briefing.

item.title: Humaiun: Bangladesh views Makkah Defence Agreement positively
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Saturday said Bangladesh was positively considering the Makkah Defence Agreement, with any decision to be guided by national interests and the potential contribution of the country's peacekeeping expertise to regional peace and stability.
“We are having positive discussions on the Makkah Defence Agreement. We are viewing it positively,” he said while addressing a national seminar at the Foreign Service Academy in the capital.
Kobir said Bangladesh could take a favourable decision if the agreement served its national interests and its peacekeeping expertise could contribute to the welfare of Muslim nations and help maintain peace and stability in the Middle East.
“If it falls within the national interests of Bangladesh and converges, and we feel that our peacekeeping expertise can add value in serving Muslim nations and keeping a stable, peaceful Middle East, then there is every scope to take a positive decision on the matter,” he said.
The Bangladesh Institute of International and Strategic Studies (BIISS) and the Center for Migration Studies of North South University (NSU) jointly organised the seminar titled “From Workforce to Strategic Partnership: Reimagining Bangladesh-KSA Relations.”
The state minister also said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had accepted an invitation from Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince to visit the Kingdom.
“He has accepted and will do so at some point very soon,” Kobir said.
He said the Crown Prince had also expressed interest in visiting Bangladesh, adding that Dhaka would welcome him at a mutually convenient time.
Kobir said the proposed visits reflected growing political ties between the two countries. He also described Bangladesh as a strong partner of Saudi Arabia in maritime security.
Calling for a comprehensive economic and strategic partnership, he said bilateral relations should expand beyond their traditional focus on labour migration and remittances.
“While that foundation remains important, it cannot be the ceiling of our ambition,” he said.
He said Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 and Bangladesh's economic transformation had created common interests in investment, human capital, technology and connectivity.
Discussions were underway on a possible investment fund to facilitate joint investments and partnerships in priority sectors, he added.
The state minister identified renewable energy, infrastructure, ports, logistics, agriculture, fisheries, food security, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, information technology and artificial intelligence as promising areas for Saudi investment.
He said such investments required a predictable and transparent business environment, improved institutional coordination and timely decision-making.
Kobir stressed the need to shift towards trained and certified professionals to meet the changing demands of Saudi Arabia's labour market.
He called for stronger cooperation among training institutions, universities and industries to ensure skills certification aligned with Saudi market requirements.
The welfare, dignity and rights of Bangladeshi workers in Saudi Arabia would remain a government priority, he said.
Kobir also highlighted opportunities for knowledge and technology partnerships, alongside cooperation in ports, shipping, logistics, aviation and supply chains.
“The next chapter of Bangladesh-Saudi Arabia relations should therefore be defined by value creation rather than volume alone,” he said.
Saudi Arabia’s Ambassador to Bangladesh Dr Abdullah Zafer bin Abiyah addressed the seminar as the guest of honour. Foreign Ministry Secretary (Bilateral) Dr Md Nazrul Islam and Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Secretary Md Mokhtar Ahmed spoke as special guests.
BIISS Director General Major General A S M Ridwanur Rahman and NSU Vice-Chancellor Professor Abdul Hannan Chowdhury also addressed the seminar.
Speaking to journalists after the event, Kobir reiterated that peace and stability in the Middle East and the Muslim world were central to Bangladesh's consideration of the Makkah Defence Agreement.
He said maintaining peace in the region encompassing Makkah and Madinah was a key objective, adding that Bangladesh could deploy its peacekeeping expertise more effectively and extensively across the world.
He said initiatives regarding participation in the agreement or association with the alliance were being considered positively, with regional peace and stability remaining the priority.
Kobir said regular high-level exchanges, including ministerial and official visits in both directions, were strengthening bilateral engagement.
He also stressed the need to diversify employment opportunities into energy, technology and other promising sectors while sending more highly skilled professionals to Saudi Arabia.
“We are also holding very positive discussions with Saudi Arabia and, God willing, many new opportunities will emerge between the two countries,” he said.
The state minister said there was scope for a broad investment partnership under which Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia could jointly invest in profitable sectors.
“The days of dependency are over. We are now placing emphasis on an equal partnership between the two countries and on sustainable policies,” he told journalists.

item.title: কেন এপেক্স ফুডসের শেয়ারের দাম সবচেয়ে বেশি বাড়ল
item.description:
শেয়ারবাজারে তালিকাভুক্ত এপেক্স ফুডসের মুনাফা এক বছরে বেড়ে দ্বিগুণের বেশি হয়েছে। তাতে গত সপ্তাহজুড়ে শেয়ারবাজারে মূল্যবৃদ্ধির শীর্ষে উঠে গেছে কোম্পানিটির শেয়ার। কোম্পানিটির শেয়ারের দাম এক সপ্তাহের ব্যবধানে ৬৯ টাকা বা প্রায় ২৭ শতাংশ বেড়েছে।

দেশের প্রধান শেয়ারবাজার ঢাকা স্টক এক্সচেঞ্জের (ডিএসই) সাপ্তাহিক বাজার পর্যালোচনায় এ চিত্র পাওয়া গেছে। গত সপ্তাহে এপেক্স ফুডস সর্বশেষ ২০২৫–২৬ অর্থবছরের আর্থিক প্রতিবেদন প্রকাশ করেছে। পাশাপাশি অর্থবছর শেষে শেয়ারধারীদের জন্য লভ্যাংশও ঘোষণা করে কোম্পানিটি। আর্থিক প্রতিবেদনে কোম্পানিটি এক বছরের ব্যবধানে উল্লেখযোগ্য মুনাফার তথ্য প্রকাশ করে। আর তাতে বাজারে কোম্পানিটির শেয়ারের প্রতি বিনিয়োগকারীদের বাড়তি আগ্রহ তৈরি হয়। তাতে শেয়ারের দামও উল্লেখযোগ্য পরিমাণে বেড়ে যায়।

আর্থিক প্রতিবেদনের তথ্য অনুযায়ী, গত জুনে সমাপ্ত ২০২৫–২৬ অর্থবছর শেষে কোম্পানিটি মুনাফা করেছে ৮ কোটি টাকার বেশি। তার আগের অর্থবছরে যার পরিমাণ ছিল ৩ কোটি ৬৫ লাখ টাকা। সে হিসাবে এক বছরের ব্যবধানে কোম্পানিটির মুনাফা বেড়েছে ৪ কোটি টাকা বা দ্বিগুণের বেশি। মুনাফার পাশাপাশি বেড়েছে প্রকৃত সম্পদমূল্য বা এনএভিও।

৪ অক্টোবর কোম্পানিটির পরিচালনা পর্ষদের সভায় গত অর্থবছরের আর্থিক প্রতিবেদন চূড়ান্ত করা হয়। একই সভা থেকে অর্থবছর শেষে শেয়ারধারীদের জন্য ২০ শতাংশ নগদ লভ্যাংশ ঘোষণা করা হয়েছে। ৫ অক্টোবর আর্থিক প্রতিবেদন ও লভ্যাংশের তথ্য দেশের দুই স্টক এক্সচেঞ্জের মাধ্যমে বিনিয়োগকারীদের জানিয়েছে কোম্পানিটি। তাতে ওই দিন একলাফে কোম্পানিটির প্রতিটি শেয়ারের দাম ৫১ টাকা বা প্রায় ২০ শতাংশ বেড়ে যায়। শেয়ারের মূল্যবৃদ্ধির সেই ধারা অব্যাহত থাকে পরবর্তী দুই কার্যদিবসেও। তাতে লভ্যাংশ ঘোষণার পর তিন কার্যদিবসে কোম্পানিটির শেয়ারের বাজারমূল্য বেড়েছে ৭৯ টাকা। এরপর গত বৃহস্পতিবার প্রতিটি শেয়ারের দাম ১১ টাকা কমেছে। তা সত্ত্বেও গত সপ্তাহ শেষে ঢাকার বাজারে মূল্যবৃদ্ধির শীর্ষে জায়গা করে নেয় কোম্পানিটি।

এপেক্স ফুডস জানিয়েছে, গত অর্থবছরে তাদের ব্যবসা থেকে আয় উল্লেখযোগ্য পরিমাণ বেড়েছে। এ কারণে বছর শেষে মুনাফায়ও বড় ধরনের প্রবৃদ্ধি হয়। একই সঙ্গে কোম্পানিটির শেয়ারবাজারের বিভিন্ন শেয়ারে যে বিনিয়োগ রয়েছে, সেসব শেয়ারের মূল্যবৃদ্ধির কারণে কোম্পানিটির সম্পদমূল্যও উল্লেখযোগ্য পরিমাণ বেড়েছে।

* সপ্তাহের ব্যবধানে বাজারে সূচক কমেছে ৫৬ পয়েন্ট।* দৈনিক গড় লেনদেন কমেছে ২১ শতাংশের বেশি।* মূল্যবৃদ্ধিতে স্বল্পমূলধনি কোম্পানির দাপট।

বাজারসংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তিরা বলছেন, ১৯৮১ সালে শেয়ারবাজারে তালিকাভুক্ত এপেক্স ফুডস খুবই স্বল্পমূলধনি কোম্পানি। ফলে বাজারে এটির শেয়ারের সংখ্যা খুবই কম। এ অবস্থায় কোম্পানিটির মুনাফা দ্বিগুণের বেশি বেড়ে যাওয়ার খবরে শেয়ারের দাম হু হু করে বেড়ে গেছে।

ডিএসইর তথ্য অনুযায়ী, এপেক্স ফুডসের মূলধন ৫ কোটি ৭০ লাখ টাকা, যা ১০ টাকা অভিহিত মূল্যের ৫৭ লাখ শেয়ারে বিভক্ত। এ শেয়ারের মধ্যে ৩০ লাখের বেশি শেয়ার রয়েছে কোম্পানির উদ্যোক্তা–পরিচালকদের হাতে। নিয়ম অনুযায়ী, উদ্যোক্তাদের হাতে থাকা এ শেয়ার ঘোষণা ছাড়া বিক্রি করা যায় না। ফলে বাজারে নিয়মিত লেনদেনযোগ্য শেয়ার রয়েছে ২৭ লাখের মতো। ফলে অল্প কিছু শেয়ারের লেনদেনে বাজারে দামও হু হু করে বেড়ে যায় বলে জানান বাজারসংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তিরা।

ডিএসইর তথ্য অনুযায়ী, শেয়ারের মূল্যবৃদ্ধির পাশাপাশি গত সপ্তাহ শেষে ঢাকার বাজারে লেনদেনের দিক থেকে শীর্ষ ১০ কোম্পানির মধ্যে ৯ম অবস্থানে ছিল এপেক্স ফুডস। সপ্তাহের ৫ কার্যদিবসে প্রতিদিন গড়ে ১০ কোটি টাকার সমমূল্যের শেয়ারের হাতবদল হয়েছে কোম্পানিটির।

এ ছাড়া ঢাকার বাজারে গত সপ্তাহ শেষে মূল্যবৃদ্ধির শীর্ষ ৫ কোম্পানির তালিকায় দ্বিতীয় থেকে পঞ্চম অবস্থানে ছিল যথাক্রমে বিডিল্যাম্পস, আজিজ পাইপস, সোনালী লাইফ ইনস্যুরেন্স ও সোনালী আঁশ। এর মধ্যে বিডিল্যাম্পসের শেয়ারের দাম ৫ কার্যদিবসে ৩৯ টাকা বা ১৭ শতাংশ, আজিজ পাইপসের দাম ১০ টাকা বা ১৩ শতাংশ, সোনালী লাইফ ইনস্যুরেন্সের দাম ১১ টাকা বা সাড়ে ১২ শতাংশ ও সোনালী আঁশের দাম ২৭ টাকা বা সোয়া ১২ শতাংশ বেড়েছে। মূল্যবৃদ্ধির শীর্ষ পাঁচ কোম্পানির সব কটিই মূলত স্বল্পমূলধনি।

এদিকে, ঢাকার বাজারে গত সপ্তাহ শেষে সূচক ও লেনদেন উভয়ই কমেছে। ডিএসইর প্রধান সূচক ডিএসইএক্স আগের সপ্তাহের চেয়ে ৫৬ পয়েন্ট কমে দাঁড়িয়েছে ৫ হাজার ৪৭৬ পয়েন্টে। সূচকের চেয়ে লেনদেন কমে গেছে উল্লেখযোগ্য পরিমাণে। গত সপ্তাহ শেষে ঢাকার বাজারে দৈনিক গড় লেনদেন আগের সপ্তাহের চেয়ে ২১ শতাংশ কমে নেমে এসেছে ৫৫৬ কোটি টাকায়। তার আগের সপ্তাহে ডিএসইতে দৈনিক গড় লেনদেনের পরিমাণ ছিল ৭০৬ কোটি টাকা।

item.title: Rooppur nuclear power plant begins fission, moves closer to electricity generation
item.description:
The first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has begun a nuclear fission reaction, bringing Bangladesh’s only nuclear power plant closer to starting electricity generation and supplying power to the national grid.

The reaction is the process through which nuclear energy is released and marks a crucial stage in the final preparations for electricity generation and supply. The plant is scheduled to supply 300 megawatts of electricity to the national grid in December.

According to sources at the Rooppur plant, the process of generating energy through nuclear fission was initially scheduled to begin in September. However, the schedule was delayed after defects were detected during tests of safety valves. The valves were tested under high pressure in two rounds last week. After reviewing the test results, the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) approved the start of the reaction last Thursday. Nuclear fission began at 3:34pm on Sunday.

The Rooppur project in Pabna is the largest single project in Bangladesh’s history in terms of cost. The Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission, under the Ministry of Science and Technology, is implementing the project. The state-owned Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh Limited (NPCBL), under the commission, is responsible for operating the plant.

Russian contractor Atomstroyexport is constructing two units at Rooppur, each with a capacity of 1,200 megawatts.

NPCBL Managing Director Md Zahedul Hasan told Prothom Alo that the final process leading to the start of the nuclear reaction began on Saturday after three days of preparation. The controlled reaction successfully started on Sunday.

“This brings to an end the long wait following the beginning of Bangladesh’s journey towards the peaceful use of nuclear energy in 1961. This is a major milestone for the country’s science sector,” he said.

Sources at the plant said the reactor vessel of the first unit had achieved criticality for the first time. This is a significant milestone for Bangladesh’s nuclear power programme. Following criticality, all key reactor parameters have remained within the prescribed limits, and the process is being conducted under controlled conditions.

Officials involved in the project said the start of the nuclear reaction was a major step towards connecting the plant to the national grid. The next stages will involve reactor physics tests, verification of safety systems, a gradual increase in reactor power and the completion of tests and preparations required for grid connection, in accordance with the approved commissioning programme.

Each stage must comply with the highest safety standards, approved procedures and regulatory requirements.

According to plant officials, achieving reactor criticality is not merely a technical success but also a historic recognition of Bangladesh’s capabilities in science, engineering and nuclear technology. After years of effort, the country has reached a crucial stage in connecting its first nuclear power plant to the national grid.

Reaction process likely to take 30 to 40 days

Sources at the Rooppur plant said a series of tests would be conducted following the start of the nuclear reaction. The entire process could take 30 to 40 days.

The reactor’s power output will then be increased gradually. Nuclear fuel fission will generate heat, which will be used to produce steam and drive a turbine to generate electricity.

Once the reactor begins producing energy, electricity can be supplied to the national grid when its output reaches 30 per cent of capacity. At that stage, the plant is expected to supply 300 megawatts of electricity, potentially in December.

Plant officials said trial operations could continue for seven to eight months after the initial start-up. Once electricity is supplied to the grid, Bangladesh will become the world’s 33rd country to generate nuclear power.

Rooppur was recognised as a nuclear installation after nuclear fuel arrived at the project site in October 2023. With the receipt of the fuel, Bangladesh also joined the group of countries possessing nuclear energy capabilities.
According to plant sources, once operational, the nuclear power plant will be able to supply electricity continuously at a steady rate, 24 hours a day.

The reactor will require refuelling every 18 months. A unit may remain shut down for up to two months for the removal of spent fuel, loading of fresh fuel and maintenance.

The sources said that once one unit of Rooppur became operational, it could save USD 1 billion annually in fuel imports. However, the project has already been delayed by three and a half years.

Project cost rises by Tk 260 billion


The Rooppur project was originally scheduled to run until December 2025. Its deadline has been extended twice, with the latest completion date set for June 2028.

Although the deadline has been extended under the agreement with the contractor, there is no provision to increase the project cost under that agreement. However, the rise in the dollar exchange rate has increased the project's expenses by Tk 260 billion.

The total cost of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant is now expected to reach Tk 1.39 trillion.

item.title: Secretariat to be relocated to old trade fair venue, new road to be built
item.description:
As the Secretariat will be relocated to Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, there will be no new buildings inside the Secretariat located on Abdul Gani Road in the capital.

The government made a policy decision last Wednesday to relocate the Secretariat in a meeting presided over by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

Top officials from the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, the Public Works Department, and the Department of Architecture were present at the meeting held at the Prime Minister's Office.

The following day, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works sent a letter to the Planning Commission to include a project for relocating the Secretariat in the Annual Development Programme (ADP).

An inter-ministerial meeting on this project is expected to be held at the Planning Commission next week.

According to a related source, the government aims to commence the project work as soon as possible and achieve visible progress during its tenure.

When contacted, the Chief Architect of the Department of Architecture, Asifur Rahman Bhuiyan, who attended the meeting, told Prothom Alo that three separate designs were presented by the Department of Architecture for relocating the Secretariat to Sher-e-Bangla Nagar. Everyone agreed to finalise one of the designs.

Architect Asifur Rahman Bhuiyan said that the project will be developed based on this design. The designs will also be presented at the meeting of the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC).

Past initiatives, no progress

According to information from the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, several initiatives to relocate the Secretariat to Sher-e-Bangla Nagar were taken during various periods, including under the Awami League government that was ousted in the July uprising.

In 2015, a project worth Tk 22.09 billion was initiated to relocate the Secretariat, scheduled for completion by June 2018.

It was initially planned to construct the Secretariat on 32 acres of land north of Zia Uddyan and west of the Bangladesh-China Friendship International Conference Centre, where the annual trade fair is held. The plan followed the original blueprint by Louis I. Kahn, the architect of the National Parliament Building.

During the Awami League administration, the original designs of the entire Sher-e-Bangla Nagar including the National Parliament Building by American architect Louis I. Kahn were brought to the country at the cost of 400,000 dollars. The plan was to build four main buildings with nine floors on top of fourteen-story bases.

However, the relocation did not materialise. During the interim government period of one and a half years, there was no discussion about moving the Secretariat.

Under the new BNP government, a project was undertaken to construct a 21-story building within the Secretariat at a cost of Tk 6 billion. When the project was presented at an ECNEC meeting on 26 April, it was sent back without approval.

In the meeting, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman instructed the Ministry of Housing and Public Works and the Department of Architecture to assess the possibility of relocating the Secretariat to Sher-e-Bangla Nagar.

Project worth Tk 35 billion

In the past five months, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works has held several meetings with stakeholders regarding the potential relocation site for the Secretariat. The preliminary estimated cost for implementing the project is Tk 35 billion.

After five months of review, a report was presented in front of the Prime Minister last Wednesday. Three separate designs by three teams from the Department of Architecture were shown in the meeting. One design was finalised, and based on it, the Housing Department was instructed to prepare the project.

New roads and facilities

According to the proposed design, a circular road will surround the Secretariat. A road will be constructed behind the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center. This road will exit to Mirpur Road passing by the July Uprising Museum (former Ganabhaban).

There are various establishments near the museum such as schools, hospitals, and the Ministry of Defence which may need to be relocated to accommodate this road.

The Ministry of Housing and Public Works has indicated discussions about constructing an underground road beneath the road that runs from Bijoy Sarani through Agargaon to Mirpur No. 10. The proposed Secretariat could be accessed via the upper road, while Mirpur Road can be reached using the lower road. A separate project might be undertaken for this.

According to the proposed design, each building within the Secretariat will be 12 stories tall. The buildings will be constructed in alignment with the National Parliament.

Related sources indicate that after the relocation of the Secretariat to Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, the main challenge will be traffic congestion. However, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works stated that measures will be taken to keep the area free from congestion.

A source from the Ministry of Housing and Public Works mentioned that after the Secretariat moves from Abdul Gani Road to Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, the current Secretariat could be repurposed for government offices such as the Dhaka Deputy Commissioner’s (DC) Office and the Superintendent of Police’s (SP) Office, currently scattered throughout Old Dhaka.

Due to limited space, the current Secretariat poses challenges for officials in carrying out office work effectively and causes heavy traffic congestion around it, leading to wasted working hours. The current Secretariat covers 1.7 million square feet, while the proposed design plans for a 3.1 million square feet area.

The trade fair ground belongs to the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, and the trade fair was moved to Purbachal in 2021, leaving the ground vacant. Four years ago, a project was undertaken to build a park on the vacant land at a cost of Tk 1 billion, although the project did not come to fruition.

Traffic congestion could be severe

The Ministry of Housing and Public Works believes that leaving the area vacant could lead to unauthorised occupation. If the Secretariat is relocated, it would prevent the land from being encroached upon.

Architect Iqbal Habib opines that relocating the Secretariat to Sher-e-Bangla Nagar following Louis I. Kahn's 1969 design would be inappropriate in 2026. He suggests considering alternative sites for relocation, similar to Putrajaya in Malaysia.

Iqbal Habib mentioned that numerous government facilities have already emerged in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar and Agargaon, increasing the number of vehicles in the area. Establishing the Secretariat there could lead to severe traffic congestion.

item.title: Rooppur plant initiates nuclear reaction for first time
item.description:
The Ministry of Science and Technology has announced that a nuclear reaction has been successfully initiated at the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant.
The reaction began for the first time at around 3:30pm on Sunday, the ministry said.
A ministry official said several days would be needed to ensure the reaction remained stable, followed by a series of tests at different stages of the plant’s commissioning.
The plant could begin generating electricity from November 20, the official added.
Located in Ishwardi, Pabna, Rooppur is Bangladesh’s first nuclear power project. It has two VVER-1200 reactors, which are expected to generate a combined 2,400MW of electricity once both units are operational.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,162 as seven die in 24 hours
item.description:
Seven more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Sunday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,162.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all seven of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,058, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 104, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the seven new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in the Sylhet division with three deaths, while Sunamganj district recorded the highest district-level death count with two casualties.
A total of 1,180 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Sunday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 205,028.
During the same period, 93 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 22,421.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 182,047 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 174,469 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Dengue: Four more die, 2,193 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Four people died of dengue, and 2,193 were hospitalized after being infected with dengue in the last 24 hours till 8am on Sunday, according to a regular report by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
With four deaths in the past 24 hours, the death toll from the disease stood at 303 this year.
Of the newly hospitalized dengue patients, 1,030 were in Dhaka Division, 70 in Mymensingh Division, 293 in Chittagong Division, 304 in Khulna Division, 160 in Rajshahi, 84 in Rangpur Division, 236 in Barisal Division and 16 in Sylhet Division.
According to the report, a total of 99,275 dengue patients have so far been hospitalized across the country this year.
However, in the last 24 hours, 1,796 patients recovered and were discharged from hospitals.
So far, 92,803 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment in hospitals.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the disease last year.

item.title: 109 migrants dead, 116 missing in boat wreck off Djibouti
item.description:
At least 109 migrants died, including 15 children, and some 116 went missing when a boat sank off the shores of Djibouti overnight on October 8-9, a UN agency said Sunday.
Survivors said the vessel -- which was carrying 305 people from Djibouti to Yemen -- capsized north of the Djibouti town of Obock, according to a statement from the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
“This is a devastating loss of life. Our thoughts are with the survivors and the families who have lost loved ones or remain without news of their relatives,” said Alexandre Coissac, IOM chief of mission in Djibouti, in the statement.
He said IOM teams were on the ground alongside Djiboutian authorities to provide emergency aid.
“This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities” by trying to cross the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Yemen and then to reach Gulf countries.
Among the 109 bodies recovered were 52 men, 42 women and 15 children -- nine girls and six boys -- the statement said.
More than 80 people survived the shipwreck, all Ethiopian nationals.
“Poverty, insecurity and the growing impacts of climate change drive many to undertake this journey, despite mounting instability across the Middle East,” the IOM said.
Yemen is stricken by fighting between the Saudi-backed government and Tehran-backed Houthi rebels, who have joined in the regional conflict involving the US and its allies against Iran.
IOM said it was assisting 64 survivors at a migrant centre in Obock.
“Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations as fears grow for those still missing.”
Since September 10, the IOM detected more than 20,000 crossings to Djibouti from Ethiopia.
In 2025, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along the sea route to Yemen and the number attempting the journey increased by 18 percent, it said.
A shipwreck in March 2026 left nine people dead and 45 missing.
IOM spokesman Kennedy Omondi Okoth told AFP this week that most of the people attempting the journey were from Ethiopia or Somalia.
He said many of them were ending up stuck in Djibouti.
The IOM urged “donors and partners to strengthen support for Djibouti’s response, including search and rescue operations and life-saving assistance”.

item.title: Pennsylvania shooting kills 9, including suspect
item.description:
Nine people, including two young children and a pregnant woman, were killed in a shooting at a residence in Erie, Pennsylvania, on Friday, with the suspected gunman dying from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said Saturday.
According to NBC News and USA TODAY, the victims included seven family members of the 45-year-old suspected shooter and a family friend. The victims ranged in age from 22 months to 51 years, according to police accounts.
Erie police received a gunshot detection alert at about 4:52pm Friday and responded to a residence on the 700 block of Perry Street. Police Chief Rick Lorah said officers arrived about three minutes after the alert and found two women, aged 51 and 37, fatally wounded outside the house.
Investigators reviewing a neighbour’s doorbell camera footage found that the women appeared distressed as they approached the residence and knocked on the door seeking assistance. Audio from the footage appeared to capture muffled gunfire from inside the house before the suspect came outside and shot the women as they ran towards him, Lorah said.
The suspect then returned inside the residence. Police reported no further gunshots after officers arrived.
Officers initially could not establish contact with anyone inside the house. According to a statement from the Erie city government cited by USA TODAY, police secured the area before a special weapons and tactics (SWAT) team entered and cleared the residence.
The officers initially saw no movement inside and heard no gunshots or cries for help. Police said they had limited information about whether the suspect remained inside or posed an ongoing threat. The city clarified that the deaths occurred before officers entered the house and that the incident did not involve a prolonged standoff or a delay caused by obtaining a search warrant.
After deploying a robot to assess the scene, officers entered the residence and found several victims. A 5-year-old boy and a 22-month-old girl were found on the first floor, while four other victims — women aged 24 and 44 and men aged 19 and 21 — were discovered in a stairwell on the second floor.
The suspected shooter, a 45-year-old man whose identity had not been publicly released, was found dead on the second floor. Police recovered a .40-caliber handgun registered to him, Lorah said.
One of the victims found inside the house was eight months pregnant. Police said the victims found inside lived at the residence, while the two women killed outside did not. One of the women was a family friend, while the other was related to a family member, according to police accounts.
Erie County Coroner Lyell Cook said his office was working to confirm the identities of the deceased. Authorities had not publicly released their names or announced final determinations on the causes of death as of Saturday afternoon, USA TODAY reported.
Lorah described the scene as the worst he had encountered during his law enforcement career. He said investigators were examining evidence, reviewing cellphones and interviewing relatives and witnesses to establish what led to the shooting.
Although the police chief said mental health could be a factor, he stressed that investigators had not established a motive. He also noted that police had previously had contact with the suspected shooter, with the last interaction he recalled occurring in 2022.
Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro said he had spoken with Erie Mayor Daria Devlin and offered the state government’s support to the victims’ families and the wider community.
“My heart breaks for this family,” Shapiro wrote on social media, adding that he and his wife were praying for the victims’ loved ones and the Erie community.
Devlin said the city was coordinating with crisis services, behavioural health providers, schools and community organisations to provide support to affected residents. Erie County District Attorney Elizabeth Hirz also urged the public to avoid spreading rumours and unverified information while the investigation continues.
The shooting occurred on the same weekend that two Philadelphia police officers were shot early Saturday. Shapiro described the incidents as a dark day for Pennsylvania.
Erie is located about 190 kilometres north of Pittsburgh.

item.title: Flash flood sweeps away 65 houses in Nepal, 5 missing
item.description:
Five people are missing after a flash flood swept away 65 houses and damaged four bridges along Nepal’s Budhi Gandaki River in the central part of the country on Sunday, according to reports by AP.
The flood struck Gorkha and Dhading districts after a landslide at Chumanubri Rural Municipality in Gorkha temporarily blocked the river, according to the Nepal Army. The river later breached the blockage, sending a sudden surge of water, mud, and debris through settlements along its banks.
Armed Police Force spokesperson Netra Bahadur Karki said all five missing people were reported from Gorkha district, adding that authorities were still collecting information about the extent of the damage.
The flood destroyed two motorable bridges and two suspension bridges, disrupting local connectivity.
The Nepal Army airlifted 36 people to safer locations following the disaster, while security forces continued search and rescue operations.
The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority evacuated residents from vulnerable areas and urged people living nearby to move to safer locations. Authorities also warned residents to remain vigilant as the situation developed.
Videos circulating on social media showed floodwaters rushing through steep mountain valleys, carrying away houses and other structures. The full extent of the damage and the number of affected settlements remained unclear.
The flooding also raised concerns in Arughat, a riverside town along a highway connecting Kathmandu with other parts of the country, where social media posts indicated that warnings had prompted evacuations.
The Budhi Gandaki River flows into the Trishuli River, an important waterway near Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu.
The disaster comes as Nepal continues to recover from devastating floods in August along its mountainous border with China, which reportedly left more than 1,400 people dead and thousands missing.
Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s office subsequently announced the end of search and rescue operations for additional victims of the earlier disaster, with authorities shifting their focus to recovery and reconstruction. Damaged roads and bridges, particularly in remote areas, have hampered the delivery of relief supplies.
The government estimates that reconstruction following the earlier floods will cost $4.77 billion. Nearly 33,000 people were affected, while about 7,500 houses were damaged or destroyed.

মেহেরপুরের গাংনী উপজেলার রংমহল সীমান্ত দিয়ে নারী ও পুরুষসহ ছয়জনকে বাংলাদেশে পুশ-ইনের চেষ্টা করেছে ভারতীয় সীমান্তরক্ষী বাহিনী (বিএসএফ)। তবে বর্ডার গার্ড বাংলাদেশের (বিজিবি) শক্ত প্রতিরোধে তাদের বাংলাদেশে প্রবেশের চেষ্টা ব্যর্থ হয়।
শনিবার (১১ অক্টোবর) ভোর ৫টার দিকে আন্তর্জাতিক সীমান্তের ১২৭ নম্বর পিলারসংলগ্ন এলাকা দিয়ে তাদের বাংলাদেশে পাঠানোর চেষ্টা করা হয়। খবর পেয়ে স্থানীয় গ্রামবাসীদের সহযোগিতায় সীমান্তে টহলরত বিজিবি সদস্যরা তাদের প্রবেশে বাধা দেন।
কুষ্টিয়া ৪৭ বিজিবি ব্যাটালিয়নের অধিনায়ক লেফটেন্যান্ট কর্নেল রাশেন হাসান রনি জানান, দিঘলকান্দি বিএসএফ ক্যাম্পের কমান্ডার হিমমত সিংয়ের নেতৃত্বে বিএসএফ সদস্যরা চার নারী ও দুই পুরুষকে বাংলাদেশে পুশইনের চেষ্টা করেন। বিষয়টি বুঝতে পেরে রংমহল বিজিবি ক্যাম্পের টহল দল প্রতিরোধ গড়ে তোলে। পরে বিজিবির বাধার মুখে তাদের ফিরিয়ে নেয় বিএসএফ।
তিনি আরও জানান, সীমান্তে বিজিবি কঠোর অবস্থানে রয়েছে। কোনোভাবেই পুশইন গ্রহণযোগ্য নয়। এ সময় তিনি স্থানীয় বাসিন্দাদের সতর্ক থাকার আহ্বান জানান।

item.description:
বাংলাদেশ সেনাবাহিনী ও সেনাপ্রধান জেনারেল ওয়াকার-উজ-জামানকে জড়িয়ে বিভিন্ন অনলাইন প্ল্যাটফর্ম ও সামাজিক যোগাযোগমাধ্যমে বিভ্রান্তিকর, ভিত্তিহীন ও উদ্দেশ্যপ্রণোদিত তথ্য প্রচার করা হচ্ছে বলে জানিয়েছে আন্তঃবাহিনী জনসংযোগ পরিদপ্তর (আইএসপিআর)। এ ধরনের বিভ্রান্তিকর ও অপপ্রচারে প্রভাবিত না হওয়ার অনুরোধ জানানো হয়েছে।

শনিবার রাতে এক সংবাদ বিজ্ঞপ্তিতে আইএসপিআর এ অনুরোধ জানিয়েছে।

সংবাদ বিজ্ঞপ্তিতে আইএসপিআর জানিয়েছে, মূলত এসব তথ্যের মাধ্যমে জনমনে বিভ্রান্তি সৃষ্টি এবং সেনাবাহিনীর ভাবমূর্তি ক্ষুণ্ন করার অপচেষ্টা চালানো হচ্ছে।

বিভ্রান্তিকর ও অপপ্রচারে প্রভাবিত না হওয়ার অনুরোধ জানিয়ে সংবাদ বিজ্ঞপ্তিতে বলা হয়েছে, সুদৃঢ় চেইন অব কমান্ড, পারস্পরিক আস্থা, ঐক্য, শৃঙ্খলা ও পেশাদারত্বের ভিত্তিতে বাংলাদেশ সেনাবাহিনী সর্বদা ঐক্যবদ্ধ রয়েছে। দেশ ও জনগণের প্রতি অর্পিত দায়িত্ব পালনে সেনাবাহিনী দৃঢ়প্রতিজ্ঞ।

এ ছাড়া বাংলাদেশ সেনাবাহিনী ও সেনাবাহিনী প্রধান সম্পর্কিত যেকোনো তথ্যের ক্ষেত্রে আনুষ্ঠানিক ও নির্ভরযোগ্য তথ্যসূত্র অনুসরণ করার আহ্বান জানানো হয়েছে বিজ্ঞপ্তিতে।

item.title: জ্যেষ্ঠ সাংবাদিক আমির খসরুর ইন্তেকাল
item.description:
ভয়েস অব আমেরিকার (ভিওএ) সাবেক বাংলাদেশ প্রতিনিধি আমির খসরু আর নেই। আজ শনিবার সন্ধ্যা ৭টায় বাংলাদেশ মেডিকেল ইউনিভার্সিটিতে চিকিৎসাধীন অবস্থায় তিনি ইন্তেকাল করেন (ইন্না লিল্লাহি ওয়া ইন্না ইলাইহি রাজিউন)। তাঁর বয়স হয়েছিল ৬২ বছর। তিনি স্ত্রী, এক ছেলে, এক মেয়েসহ আত্মীয়স্বজন ও শুভানুধ্যায়ী রেখে গেছেন।

আমির খসরু দীর্ঘদিন ধরে কিডনি ও লিভারের নানা জটিলতায় ভুগছিলেন। মস্তিষ্কে রক্তক্ষরণ হওয়ায় এক সপ্তাহ ধরে হাসপাতালের নিবিড় পরিচর্যা কেন্দ্রে (আইসিইউ) ছিলেন।

আমির খসরু দৈনিক ইত্তেফাক-এর কূটনৈতিক সাংবাদিক হিসেবে দীর্ঘদিন দায়িত্ব পালন করেছেন। এ ছাড়া তিনি কর্মজীবনে সংবাদ, দৈনিক খবর, চ্যানেল আইসহ বিভিন্ন গণমাধ্যমে কাজ করেছেন। আজকের বুধবার নামে একটি সাপ্তাহিক পত্রিকা সম্পাদনা করা ছাড়াও বিভিন্ন জাতীয় পত্রিকায় কলাম লিখতেন।

আমির খসরু ছিলেন ওভারসিজ করেসপনডেন্টস অ্যাসোসিয়েশনের (ওকাব) সাবেক সভাপতি ও সাধারণ সম্পাদক। ছিলেন রিপোর্টার্স ফোরাম ফর ইলেকশন অ্যান্ড ডেমোক্রেসির (আরএফইডি) প্রতিষ্ঠাতা সভাপতি এবং জাতীয় প্রেসক্লাব ও ঢাকা রিপোর্টার্স ইউনিটির স্থায়ী সদস্য।

পারিবারিক সূত্রে জানা গেছে, কাল রোববার লালমাটিয়া মসজিদে, জাতীয় প্রেসক্লাব প্রাঙ্গণে ও রিপোর্টার্স ইউনিটিতে জানাজা শেষে মিরপুর বুদ্ধিজীবী কবরস্থানে তাঁকে দাফন করা হবে।

item.title: Trump, Putin reach deal to release Russian diesel to world
item.description:
US President Donald Trump on Friday said Russian President Vladimir Putin had agreed to release Russian diesel to US and global markets.
The move, which aims to address rising fuel costs before the US midterm elections, marks a dramatic turnaround in US policy toward Moscow since the start of the war in Ukraine.
In a social media post, Trump wrote he had made a deal with Putin during a phone call that was supposed to be about a suspected plague outbreak in Russia.
According to Trump, Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons “immediately thereafter.”
Trump wrote that Russia would deliver another 3 million tons “within a short period of time” after that.
The US Treasury Department issued a temporary license that will allow Russian diesel to reach global markets through April 2027.
Trump’s announcement follows his signing of a broad Russia sanctions law last month. The law is intended to clamp down on Russia’s energy sector and other areas that fuel its war against Ukraine.
Kirill Dmitriev, the Russian presidential envoy, reposted the Treasury Department’s announcement on X, saying that “Russia-US cooperation on diesel and energy will benefit the world.”
Alexander Novak, Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister, said that the country was ready to start supplying additional volumes of diesel to the United States and other countries from October.
He also said that Russia’s exports are expected to rise further in November and December as refineries resume operations after maintenance.
Later, the Kremlin released a statement from Putin saying that, during their call, he and Trump had also devoted “significant attention to the prospects of resolving the Ukrainian crisis” and had discussed “the situation around Iran and various aspects of bilateral relations.”
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has condemned the agreement, saying that any easing of sanctions without a clear and lasting de-escalation agreement with Russia is an obvious sign of “weakness.”
“Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world. Russia will ‘repay’ the diesel with further terror and perfidy,” he wrote on social media.
“Allowing Russia to ⁠sell ​petroleum products ​is an investment in a ​war that ‌must be ended, not prolonged. What ​is needed ⁠is real de-escalation with Russia ⁠on ​a reciprocal basis,” the Ukrainian president stressed.
Zelensky added that Ukraine hopes the US will have a strong conversation with Russia: “A strong one, not a weak one.”
Since its 2022 full-scale invasion of neighboring Ukraine, Moscow has been hit with rounds of sanctions by the United States and its Western partners.
But as the war has continued with no resolution in sight, Washington’s commitment to that approach has appeared to waver.
Earlier this year, temporary US sanctions waivers that allowed the sale of Russian oil raised concerns because they could hinder efforts to deprive Moscow of funds for its war in Ukraine.
Last month, Trump blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries for soaring diesel prices, and even publicly told Zelensky to stop the attacks.
Trump’s announcement on Friday came just as US, Ukrainian, and European officials were meeting in Miami for new diplomatic talks aimed at ending Russia’s war in Ukraine.

item.title: US announces sanctions on the International Criminal Court
item.description:
US President Donald Trump’s administration imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday, hours after one of its former judges won the Nobel Peace Prize.
This comes as the US has in recent months made no bones about pursuing what Secretary of State Marco Rubio has called a “sweeping campaign to dismantle the threat posed by the International Criminal Court.”
The United States and Israel had both strongly opposed the court’s arrest warrants for top Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Since 2020 and the back end of Trump’s first term, the US had also opposed investigations into military actions in Afghanistan that “deprioritize” alleged US wrongdoings, focusing on the Taliban, but can nevertheless include them.
“President Trump will never allow the International Court to prosecute Americans,” Rubio said in a statement.
“That is why, today, the United States is sanctioning the International Criminal Court. We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate,” he said.
Rubio said that both US political parties had long agreed that the ICC should not have jurisdiction over US citizens, but said “only President Trump” resolved to take action.
“Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC. We expect our allies, many of whom are part of the ICC and that rely on American servicemembers for their defense, to rein in the court,” Rubio said. “If they do not, the United States will continue its campaign to dismantle the ICC, brick by brick, until Americans are threatened no longer.”
The ICC said the US sanctions aimed to obstruct an independent international court supported by more than half of the UN’s members.
“The court will continue to fully discharge its mandate, with independence and impartiality, acting only on the basis of the law and the evidence, for the sake of the countless victims of grave crimes,” said ICC President Tomoko Akane, who already faces US sanctions.
The ICC called the Rome Statute, which underpins membership of the court, a “collective promise” that the most serious international crimes must not go unpunished.
“That promise is only as strong as the resolve of those who made it,” the court said. It appealed to members to take “concrete actions” to ensure the court would still have the necessary means to continue its work.
“No one should be punished for serving the cause of justice,” it said. “History will judge this moment. Future generations, and above all the victims of mass atrocities, will ask how we responded when an insitution created to protect them came under attack.”
A collection of US allies that are full members of the ICC including Germany issued a joint statement reaffirming their “continued and unwavering support for the independence, impartiality, and integrity of the ICC.”
“As committed supporters of the ICC we regret and strongly disagree with the announcement of sanctions to be imposed upon the Court by the United States,” the governments of Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands and the UK said.
They said that, despite the ICC’s best efforts to prepare and mitigate their effect, the sanctions “will have a significant impact on the Court’s work, its dedicated staff and their families.”
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu thanked the US government for its “leadership” in issuing the sanctions.
“The ICC is not a court. It is a political body that poses a mortal threat to law abiding democracies worldwide and to the very idea of national sovereignty,” he said.
The State Department released the announcement a few hours after the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navi Pillay, who was an ICC judge from 2003 to 2012.
Last year Trump repeatedly complained that he should have won the accolade for promoting world peace, prompting Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado to present him with her trophy as a gift.
Without naming names, the Nobel Committee clearly referenced US sanctions against the ICC when announcing Pillay as this year’s laureate.
“The Norwegian Nobel Committee wants to remind the world that the rule of law national and international — underpins the system we have set up to ensure peace and resolve conflicts non-violently,” the Committee wrote.
It said judges like Pillay “guard the thin red line between order and chaos,” but lamented that “today ... these same judges are sanctioned, and their institutions are attacked.” The International Criminal Court is an intergovernmental organization and international tribunal based in the Dutch city of The Hague.
It’s the only permanent international court with the theoretical jurisdiction to prosecute individuals for international crimes like genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and illegal aggression.
The ICC was established in 2002 and is governed by the Rome Statute.
More than half the countries in the world, 125 in total, are full parties to the Rome Statute, having signed and ratified it.
Several of the world’s most significant powers, including China, India, Israel, Russia and the United States, do not recognize the court’s jurisdiction and are not parties to the statute.
A grey area, however, remains since the court accepts challenges from ratified members against individuals from countries that do not recognize it.
That is why high-profile arrest warrants against Russian officials, including President Vladimir Putin, and Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, have been issued in recent years — following respective complaints from Ukrainians and Palestinians.
The US has been increasingly critical of the ICC during Trump’s second term.
Rubio has often led the charge. In July, he wrote an op-ed for the Wall Street Journal saying, “America never agreed to a world tribunal that can override our own courts and the Constitution.”
He argued it was possible for US “soldiers, police officers, Border Patrol agents and elected leaders” to be “dragged before an international court” and tried by judges “from random countries across the globe.”
Just over a week later, on July 25, Venezuela’s new administration — transformed after the US abduction of Nicolas Maduro in January — announced that it planned to withdraw from the Rome Statute and the ICC.
A few days later, the military junta in Chad announced that it was withdrawing from the ICC following a US request.
The recent sexual misconduct scandal surrounding the ICC’s chief prosecutor Karim Khan, who was dismissed in July, provided more ammunition the US could aim at the court.
In August, the US imposed sanctions on the ICC’s president, Japanese judge Tomoko Akane, and Abdoulaye Seye, a Senegalese trial lawyer at the court.

item.title: Dengue: Four more die, 1,935 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Four people died of dengue, and 1,631 were hospitalized with the Aedes mosquito-borne disease in the last 24 hours till 8am on Saturday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
With this development, the country has recorded 299 deaths from dengue this year.
Of the new dengue cases, 703 were recorded in Dhaka division, 61 in Mymensingh division, 234 in Chittagong division, 184 in Khulna division, 141 in Rajshahi division, 75 in Rangpur division, 219 in Barisal division and 14 in Sylhet division.
A total of 97,082 dengue patients have so far been hospitalized across the country this year, according to the DGHS report.
However, in the last 24 hours, 1,627 patients recovered and were discharged from hospitals.
So far, 91,007 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment this year.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the disease last year.

item.title: Abdul Awal Mintoo: Bangladesh, India to hold talks on elephant corridor in Sherpur
item.description:
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo on Saturday said the government would soon initiate talks with India under an existing protocol to establish a cross-border corridor for wild elephants roaming the Garo Hills in Sherpur.
Around 130 to 135 wild elephants that came from India's Meghalaya have become stranded in the Garo Hills of Sherpur as border fencing has prevented them from returning to their habitat, he said.
The minister said the government would request the Indian authorities to open gates in the fencing to allow the elephants to return, although previous requests had not received a positive response.
At the same time, initiatives would be taken to develop forest areas in Sherpur into safe habitats for the elephants, he added.
The minister made the remarks while speaking at a discussion on resolving human-elephant conflict and conserving wild elephants at Madhutila Eco Park in Nalitabari upazila of Sherpur.
He said the scenic Garo Hills, its wild elephants and the surrounding natural environment would be used to develop the area into a tourism hub. This would create economic opportunities for local people while helping protect elephants and reduce human-elephant conflict, he added.
The Sherpur district administration and the Mymensingh Forest Division organized the discussion with lawmakers from elephant-affected areas, Elephant Response Team (ERT) members, journalists and volunteers involved in elephant conservation. Deputy Commissioner Farida Yesmin chaired the event.
Sherpur-2 lawmaker Engineer Fahim Chowdhury, Chief Conservator of Forests Md Amir Hossain Chowdhury, Conservator of Forests for the Wildlife and Nature Conservation Region Md Sanaullah Patwari, Central Region Conservator of Forests ASM Zahir Uddin Akon, Mymensingh Divisional Forest Officer Kazi Muhammad Nurul Karim and Police Superintendent AKM Johirul Islam spoke as special guests.
